name: Shuppim
overview: Shuppim was a male member of the tribe of Levi, known specifically for his role as a gatekeeper to the west. His position highlights a responsibility within the Levitical duties, emphasizing service and guardianship related to the temple or sacred precincts. There are no additional notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shuppim appears only once in Scripture without an explicit meaning or title attached. It is presented simply as a proper name without further etymological insight or divine naming significance.
familyAndRelationships: Shuppim is identified as a descendant of Levi, situating him within the Levitical lineage. Beyond this tribal affiliation, Scripture does not record any other family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Shuppim's significance lies in his role as a gatekeeper to the west, a position entrusted to Levites who served in the maintenance and security of the sanctuary. This role reflects the broader Levitical responsibility to uphold the holiness and order of God's dwelling place. His mention in 1 Chronicles 26:16 underscores the organized structure of temple service during the post-exilic period.
